Our Ethos
Our Mission Statement is to 'Aspire not to have more but to be more' Is a clear expression of our mission to develop a Christian community where children aspire to be the best that they can be and fulfil God's work on earth. As a result our mission statement has a significant impact in all aspects of life within our schools. Our Faith is at the centre of everything we do and our aim is to foster and deepen the children's faith, to help them to enter into a personal relationship with God and to respond to Him through prayer, worship and Christian living. We try to live as Jesus would want us by showing the personal qualities of caring, sharing, love, trust, honesty and mutual respect. We strive to make our school community one in which everyone is valued and seen in the image of Christ.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Catholic Primary Schools Trust - Catholic Life and Mission
pageCache.text:
Catholic Life and Mission
Our Mission Statement is to 'Aspire not to have more but to be more' Is a clear expression of our mission to develop a Christian community where children aspire to be the best that they can be and fulfil God's work on earth. As a result, our mission statement has a significant impact in all aspects of life within our schools.
Christ at the centre of all we do
At St Mary’s Primary Schools Trust, Catholic Life and Mission is not an additional feature of school life, it is its foundation. It shapes our decisions, our relationships and the way we live and learn together as a faith-filled community.
Inspired by Christ’s Gospel, we strive to ensure that every child experiences a school environment rooted in love, dignity, forgiveness and service.
A living and active faith community
Catholic Life is visible and actively experienced throughout the school. Pupils and staff recognise that they are part of a shared mission to live out Gospel values in daily life.
Faith is expressed through prayer, worship, reflection and action. Pupils are encouraged to understand that their beliefs are not only taught but lived in their interactions, behaviour and service to others.
Pupils at the heart of mission
Pupils play an active role in shaping the Catholic Life of the school. They are encouraged to reflect on Gospel values and apply them in practical ways within school life.
They take responsibility for living out the school’s mission, contributing to a culture where kindness, respect and compassion are consistently demonstrated.
Pupil voice is valued and used to shape aspects of worship, charitable action and community life.
Faith in action through service
Catholic Life is strengthened through a clear commitment to service and social responsibility. Pupils are given opportunities to support others locally and globally, developing a strong sense of justice and compassion.
Through charitable work and lived experiences of service, pupils begin to understand their role in building a fairer and more caring world.
We encourage our children to care for God’s world and its people by developing empathy, sympathy and a desire to live out their faith through charitable works. Inspired by Laudato Si’, Pope Francis’ call to care for our common home, we help our pupils understand the importance of looking after creation and showing love and respect for all members of our global family.
A strong sense of belonging and community
St Mary’s is a welcoming and inclusive Catholic community where every child is valued and known.
Strong relationships between home, school and parish support pupils in developing a secure understanding of their faith. Parents are actively involved in the Catholic life of the school through liturgies, celebrations, shared worship experiences and charity events.
Formation of the whole child
Catholic Life at St Mary’s contributes to the spiritual, moral, social and emotional development of every pupil. It helps children to reflect on their actions, develop empathy and grow in understanding of themselves and others.
Pupils are supported to recognise their God-given talents and to use them for the good of others, both within school and beyond.
“What Would Jesus Do?”
At the heart of our Catholic Life and Mission is a simple but powerful question: “What would Jesus do?”
We encourage all members of our school community, children and staff alike, to use this question as a guide in their daily actions, decisions and relationships with others. It reminds us to live as Jesus taught us: with love, compassion, forgiveness, honesty and kindness.
This shared vision helps us to build a school community rooted in Gospel values where everyone is treated with dignity and respect. Whether in the classroom, on the playground or within the wider community, we strive to follow the example of Christ in all that we do.
All staff at the Junior Scholl wear a “What Would Jesus Do?” badge as a visible reminder of our commitment to living out our faith each day. These badges also encourage meaningful conversations with the children and help reinforce our shared responsibility to model Christ’s behaviour in every aspect of school life.
Through prayer, reflection and daily actions, we aim to ensure that our Catholic faith is not simply taught but truly lived.
How Catholic Life and Mission is lived day to day

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Catholic Primary Schools Trust - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship is central to the life and mission of St Mary’s Infant and Junior Schools. It is not an “add on” but the heartbeat of our daily rhythm, shaping the spiritual life of pupils and staff and drawing the whole community into a shared encounter with God.
Worship is rooted in Scripture, guided by the Church’s liturgical year and expressed through prayer, silence, reflection and joyful celebration. It is a lived experience that pupils understand, participate in and help to lead.
A daily experience of prayer and encounter
Collective Worship takes place every day and is carefully planned to ensure depth, variety and progression. Across the school, pupils experience:
Pupils are attentive, engaged and confident in responding to worship, whether through reading, prayer, discussion or reflection. There is a strong sense of reverence and participation throughout all year groups.
Pupil leadership and ownership
Pupils play an important role in shaping prayer and liturgy. From an early age, they are encouraged to contribute, and as they move through the school, they take on greater responsibility for planning and leading prayer and liturgy.
This develops confidence, understanding of Scripture and a deep sense of ownership of the school’s prayer life. Worship is not something done “to” pupils, but something they shape and lead.
Rooted in the Church’s liturgical year
Collective Worship follows the rhythm of the Church’s year, helping pupils to understand the story of Christ and the life of the Church.
Key feasts, seasons and celebrations are marked with reverence and joy, supporting pupils in developing a secure understanding of Catholic tradition and how it shapes daily life in school.
A prayerful and reflective community
Worship at St Mary’s is characterised by:
Pupils demonstrate a clear understanding of different ways of praying within the Catholic tradition and respond with maturity and enthusiasm.
Living out our mission
Collective Worship supports our mission to form children in faith, hope and love. It helps pupils to reflect on their actions, recognise God in their daily lives and grow in compassion for others.
Through worship, pupils learn that prayer is not confined to moments in school, but shapes how they live, learn and treat others.
Examples of our Collective Worship in action
Collective Worship at St Mary’s is purposeful, structured and deeply embedded in daily life. It forms pupils spiritually, supports their understanding of faith and builds a strong sense of Catholic identity across the whole school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Catholic Primary Schools Trust - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Trust Mission Statement “Aspire not to have more, but to be more”, is alive in our schools. It is central to everything we do and our ethos is founded upon it in our daily school lives both pupils and staff who bear witness to it.
We strive to be a community of resilience and compassion. We endeavour to live our lives like Jesus, being an example to others. To this end, our pupils are encouraged and supported to live out their faith by treating others kindly and supporting those less fortunate than themselves locally, nationally and internationally.
Our curriculum and policy are also formulated in the light of our mission statement.
Each child is valued as unique and is treated with dignity. All in our community are treated with respect, each is a valued member and our ambition for our pupils is boundless.
We want our pupils to be excellent citizens who can contribute to society. We encourage and support our community’s faith formation. We encourage our children to aspire for excellence in all things, be excellent learners and to have the confidence to access challenges whilst never losing sight of the gospel values we strive to live by.
School Day
Each school in our Trust delivers 32.5 hours of education a week. This time includes breaks, lunch, and the school day from morning registration to the official afternoon dismissal- which totals 6.5 hours a day
Infant school - 8.55am - 3.25pm
Infant Nursery -9.00am- 12.00 or 12.20pm-3.20pm
Junior School -9.00am- 3.30pm

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Catholic Primary Schools Trust - Welcome from the Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Dear Parents and Carers,
A very warm welcome to St Mary’s Catholic Infant School. I am delighted that you are considering our school for your child.
At St Mary’s, we believe that every child is a unique and precious gift from God. Rooted in the Word of God, our mission statement is 'Learning to Love, Loving to Learn'. We have high expectations for all and to provide a rich, inclusive, and purposeful curriculum that reflects the spirit of our school community. Alongside our Catholic mission, we are committed to preparing children for life in modern Britain. We actively promote British values, democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs — and weave these into our daily school life. In doing so, we help children to grow as responsible citizens, ready to contribute positively to society with respect, compassion, and integrity.
We welcome children into our Nursery at the age of three, and invite applications for a Reception Class place in the academic year that children turn five. We also have close links with our Junior School, and the majority of parents choose to apply for a Junior place in Year 3, ensuring a smooth transition for our children as they continue their learning journey.
Our approach to teaching and learning is guided by a set of core beliefs. We believe in creativity, offering opportunities for children to think freely, take risks, and express themselves across the curriculum. We value hands-on experiences that bring learning to life, spark curiosity, and nurture a love of discovery. We adapt our teaching to meet the needs of every child, enabling all to flourish and fulfil their God-given potential.
We also encourage independence and reasoning, giving children the time and space to explore their ideas, ask questions, and develop confidence in their own abilities. We value expression and voice, ensuring every child feels heard and respected in our nurturing, faith-filled environment. As a Catholic community, we foster a strong sense of belonging, identity, and service, working closely with families, our parish, and the wider community.
Our children are also encouraged to find joy and wonder in the natural world. Through regular outdoor learning, they connect with God’s creation, develop responsibility for the environment, and grow in awe and gratitude.
At St Mary’s, our curriculum is not just about what we teach, but how we teach, always with love, purpose, and the belief that every child is made in the image of God, with unique potential to grow, thrive, and shine.
I warmly invite you to contact us and arrange a tour of the school. It would be my pleasure to welcome you in person and share with you the vibrant, faith-filled community that makes St Mary’s such a special place.
With every blessing,
Please contact the school Office on 0208 688 2891 or email office@st-marys-inf.croydon.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Catholic Primary Schools Trust - Welcome from the Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Dear Parents, Carers and Families,
A very warm welcome to St Mary’s Catholic Junior School.
It is a privilege to welcome you to our school community and to continue in another exciting year together.
Since joining the school, I have had the great privilege of getting to know our children, families and staff even more closely. What has struck me most is the genuine sense of community that exists at St Mary’s. We are a school where children are known, valued and encouraged to believe in themselves and where we work together to ensure that every child has the opportunity to flourish.
At the heart of everything we do is our Catholic mission. We seek to live out the Gospel in the way we learn, work and care for one another, rooted in the values of Love, Respect, Peace and Faith. We want our children not simply to achieve academically, but to grow into compassionate, courageous and thoughtful young people who understand that they have an important role to play in their families, their communities and the wider world.
‘Fidem Serva’ — Keep the Faith — is at the heart of our identity. We encourage our children to have faith in God, faith in themselves and faith in what they can achieve.
Our ambition for every child is high. We provide a broad, rich and carefully considered curriculum which develops knowledge, vocabulary, creativity and independence, while giving children opportunities to discover their interests and talents. We celebrate academic success and are proud of the strong outcomes our pupils achieve, but we recognise that education is about so much more than results. We want our children to leave St Mary’s as confident learners, resilient problem-solvers, effective communicators and kind, responsible citizens.
This is captured in our St Mary’s Way. We want our children to be Active, Aspirational, Collaborative, Friendly, Independent, Persistent, Responsible and Versatile. These are not simply words on a wall; they are qualities we actively nurture in our pupils every day.
We also recognise that children achieve the most when schools and families work in partnership. Our relationship with parents and carers is therefore incredibly important to us. We want you to feel welcomed, listened to and confident that we are working alongside you in the best interests of your child.
As we look ahead to the year, our ambition remains simple: to provide an exceptional education within a caring, inclusive and distinctly Catholic community where every child can thrive.
Whether your child is joining us in Year 3, returning for another year or preparing for their final year at St Mary’s, I hope that they will feel a strong sense of belonging here. I hope they will be challenged to achieve more than they thought possible, supported when things are difficult and encouraged to be the very best version of themselves.
As Archbishop Oscar Romero reminds us:
“Aspire not to have more, but to be more.”
That is a wonderful aspiration for our children and for all of us.
Thank you for entrusting your children to us. I look forward to working with you and to sharing another successful, happy and memorable year at St Mary’s.
With very best wishes,
Sarah Fizul Headteacher St Mary’s Catholic Junior School
Fidem Serva — Keep the Faith

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Catholic Primary Schools Trust - Catholic Life of our Junior School
pageCache.text:
Catholic Life of our Junior School
We take pride in the prayerful way our children conduct themselves each day, and in their growing understanding of prayer as an encounter with the Lord. Prayer and Collective Worship are central to the daily life of our school and underpin everything we do.
In Year 3 is an important year for our children, as the majority receive formation in their parishes in preparation for receiving the Blessed Sacrament for the first time. They are supported in school through the ‘Come and See’ programme, as they deepen their understanding of the Sacrament of Reconciliation and the Blessed Eucharist.
In Year 4, children begin to take on greater responsibility for liturgy and Collective Worship. They plan, rehearse and present the Nativity to the rest of the school, interpreting the Gospel accounts of the Nativity of the Lord and combining these into a shared narrative that supports the prayer and reflection of the school community.
In Year 5, children are encouraged to look outward to the wider community and to share their faith through action. As part of the Mini Vinnies initiative, children work for social justice and are given opportunities to reflect on how they live out Gospel values. Older children are also encouraged to engage respectfully with other faith communities within our neighbourhood.
In Year 6, children become leaders in faith and take responsibility for leading prayer and celebration. Year 6 pupils regularly proclaim the Gospel during Collective Worship, support the celebration of others’ achievements and take a central role in leading the whole school community in the Leavers’ Mass each July.
The pattern of the week ensures that all children engage in prayer and reflection daily through planned and purposeful Collective Worship.
Each Monday, the Headteacher leads whole-school Collective Worship, rooted in the Liturgical Year. The opening prayer for the week is led by children from Years 3 and 4, and together the school asks Mary, the Patron of our school, to intercede for us. The theme reflects on the previous Sunday’s Gospel and challenges children to live out Gospel values in the week ahead.
On Tuesdays, the school gathers for a simple Liturgy, followed by hymn practice as part of our Collective Worship. Children are encouraged to reflect on the meaning of the hymns and their connection to the Church’s year or the school’s current focus. Teaching assistants plan and lead these sessions, supporting children to praise God through song.
On Wednesdays, a class teacher leads Collective Worship focused on themes drawn from Religious Education or PSHE. This takes place on a rota, ensuring that children experience prayer and reflection led by a range of staff.
Each Thursday, one class prepares and leads Collective Worship for the rest of the school, including prayer, praise and reflection. Parents and carers are warmly invited to attend, with dates shared in advance through the weekly newsletter. These celebrations alternate with a weekly Liturgy, also open to parents. Children are actively involved in planning and leading these acts of worship.
Every Friday, the school gathers for Celebration Collective Worship, led by the Head Boy and Head Girl. The Gospel for the forthcoming Sunday is proclaimed by Year 6 pupils, followed by a reflection led by the Head of School or a member of the Senior Leadership Team. Children’s achievements are celebrated, and birthdays from the week are acknowledged as part of our shared community life.
Our Faith Leaders play a key role in reaching out to the wider community and supporting children in taking responsibility for their faith journey. Each September, children vote for representatives from their class, considering which pupils are best able to serve others, support community initiatives and contribute to the spiritual life of the school.
Members of the Faith Leader team learn that communication is a shared responsibility. They are encouraged to listen attentively to others and to support their peers in bearing witness to their faith through words and actions.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Catholic Primary Schools Trust - Catholic Social Teaching
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
Our faith calls us to love God and to love our neighbours in every situation, especially those living in poverty. Following in the footsteps of Christ, we hope to make His love and peace present in our daily lives. Inspired by Fratelli Tutti, Pope Francis’ message of human fraternity and social friendship, we encourage our children to recognise the dignity of every person and to build a community rooted in kindness, compassion and solidarity.
Catholic Social Teaching is based on the belief that God has a plan for creation, a plan to build His kingdom of peace, love and justice. It provides a moral framework for addressing social issues and helps us to develop each individual child so they can contribute positively to our immediate community and the wider world.
The Catholic Church has seven principles of social teaching that we share with our children through everything we do: through the curriculum, special events, activities and through our ordinary actions in school.
At St Mary’s Catholic Primary Trust, we have chosen to focus primarily on these principles with the children across the year. As a staff, we have selected those most relevant to the children of St Mary’s, enabling them to gain a deep understanding and to demonstrate these values through their everyday lives.
HUMAN DIGNITY (Everyone is Special )
God made each person, so every life is important and should be protected.
At St Mary’s we uphold the human dignity of others in various ways:
Demonstrating respect in all our interactions.
THE COMMON GOOD (Thinking of everyone )
God made us to be part of communities, families and countries, so all people can share and help each other.
At St Mary's we show we are part of a community by:
PARTICIPATION (Sharing Fairly)
Work is important in God's plan for adults and their families, so job and pay should be fair.
At St Mary's we exemplify the importance of sharing by:
SOLIDARITY (Showing people we care)
God made everyone, so we are all brothers and sisters in God's family wherever we live.
At St Mary's we show we care about our wider community by:
OPTION FOR THE POOR (Putting people most in need first)
God wants us to help people who are poor, who don't have enough food, a safe place to live, or a community.
At St Mary's we show we are part of a community by:
Working together
Working hard to help others
Fundraising for others to help them.
CARING FOR GOD'S CREATION
The world was made by God so we take care of all creation.
At St Mary's we show we care for creation by:
Taking responsibility for our environment
